Subject: Planning: Private 2.4 upgrade window + version pinning questions

Hi Ben —

Were starting to plan the upgrade from Private 2.3.1 (pinned) -> 2.4.0 for our VPC deployment. Security asked for a short written plan covering: 
- compatibility gates (kernel, distro, Nvidia driver),
- rollback/roll-forward checks,
- proposed maintenance windows (US-PST preferred),
and whether Redwood can support a staged canary first in our pre-prod VPC.

Can you share a proposed timeline and the preflight checklist we should run? Our compliance officer also wants to see the rollback playbook (high level) before we commit a maintenance window.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Kumar
Head of Platform Engineering, SOHO Analytics

Subject: Re: Planning: Private 2.4 upgrade window + version pinning questions

Priya —

Thanks for the clear asks. At a high level we can support a staged rollout with a canary in pre-prod followed by a controlled production window. Ive attached a compact upgrade matrix and our preflight checklist. High-level plan below: 

1) Preflight (3 business days): run private_preflight_checklist.pdf against your pre-prod VPC (checks: kernel modules, driver versions, firewall rules, secrets access, KV-cache continuity).
2) Canary window (2 hours): deploy 2.4.0 to a canary pool (10% of traffic) with metrics and tracing hooks enabled.
3) Roll-forward staging (1 day): if canary OK, expand to Staging (50%) then full prod in controlled waves (25% -> 50% -> 100%) with 30-min observation gates.
4) Rollback option: if a critical regression appears, immediate automatic rollback to 2.3.1 using pinned image + warm cache fallback; manual approval for roll-forward thereafter.

Maintenance window: We propose Tue 2028-05-23 01:00-05:00 US-PST for production (low traffic). Canary could run Tue 2028-05-16 02:00-04:00 US-PST.

Open items for Redwood engineering: confirm driver compatibility matrix (NVIDIA driver >= 535.x?), confirm whether any compilation-based kernels require rebuilds for quantized runtimes. Evelyn / Dev: can you comment on the kernel/driver constraints and safe rollback timings?

Ben
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference

Attachment: upgrade_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet: version compat table)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 13 May 2028 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planning: Private 2.4 upgrade window + version pinning questions

Ben / Team / Priya —

Quick technical notes from infra runbook POV: 
- Nvidia driver: 535.54+ is supported for the new fused-kernel path; 470-series will not work for the optimized kernels but we provide a safe fallback path (slower) that does not require driver upgrade. That fallback increases token-latency by ~30% for peak sequences.
- Kernel (host): we require host kernel 5.15+ for the prebuilt toolchain; older kernels must run our compatibility shim (adds risk).
- Rollback cadence: full rollback (image pin to 2.3.1) completes within 12-18 mins for a single 20-node pool if automated; we recommend an additional 30-min buffer for KV-cache warmup and NGINX health checks.

Ive attached a short rollback_playbook_snippets.txt with the precise kubectl and terraform steps wed run; we also include a canary tracer that triggers automatic abort on error-rate > 0.5% sustained over 5m.

Evelyn
Director, Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference

Attachment: rollback_playbook_snippets.txt (mini playbook)

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 13 May 2028 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planning: Private 2.4 upgrade window + version pinning questions

Adding the engineering preflight hits: 
- Preflight checklist highlights (also in private_preflight_checklist.pdf):
  * Verify image pull secrets and repo access (10m)
  * Confirm node allocatable GPU memory >= baseline (check via nvidia-smi)
  * Run canary inference suite (20 sample prompts, compare logprobs and latency)
  * KV-cache continuity test (start small session, pause/resume, ensure cache index continuity)
  * Telemetry hooks: ensure FluentD ingestion + trace sampling at 100% for first 15m of canary, then 10%

- Known incompatibility: older distros with glibc <2.28 require a rebuilt shim; weve provided a prebuilt shim in the matrix but this implies a slightly longer rollback since shim load/unload is stateful.

Operational ask: can SOHO provide a runbook contact (privileged user) available during the maintenance window for immediate approve/abort? It helps reduce rollback latency.

Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: private_preflight_checklist.pdf (checklist doc)
